newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles leads mourning for Dunblane victims.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles leads mourning for Dunblane victims.

text.p: Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, joined hundreds of mourners on Wednesday for a moving memorial service in Dunblane Cathedral for 16 children killed by a crazed gunman at the town's primary school in March.

Parents, relatives and friends of the dead four- and five- year-olds and their teacher, Gwenne Mayor, who was also killed, wept as each victim's name was read out. A large candle was lit for each child in the centre of the vaulted protestant church.
Shops in the Scottish town closed in a mark of respect. After the carnage, the gunman, Thomas Hamilton. shot himself.
"Our act of remembrance here today used the symbolism of light. It seems so natural and appropriate," Reverend James Whyte told the mourners who filled the cathedral.
"By lighting the candles and by reading the name, you as a community have remembered before God each individual who died in the massacre on March 13.
"Each of these candles represents a unique human life. The candle is a good symbol, especially for the children. It is small, yet it is a bright, warm light."
The invitation-only service, accompanied by a full choir, was relayed to other churches in the town and broadcast live on British television.

Scottish Secretary Michael Forysth and the opposition Labour Party's spokesman for Scottish affairs, George Robertson, who lives in Dunblane, set aside their political differences to pay their respects.
The massacre by Hamilton, a loner and gun enthusiast, led to calls for an immediate ban on handguns in Britain.
Prime Minister John Major appointed a senior judge, Lord Douglas Cullen, to investigate the massacre and the question of private ownership of guns. He is expected to deliver his report next Monday.

The ruling Conservatives have dithered over the issue but Labour, which has a commanding lead in public opinion polls and is widely expected to win the next general election which must be held by May, have vowed to ban private ownership of handguns.
